Before you continue your French review, take one minute to read this message. Today’s study counts, however short it is. Your ear, your mouth and your memory adapt to French through small, steady practice repeated every day.
Verses for daily study
“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little.”
Isaiah 28:10 · KJV
Learning grows the same way: one sentence, one word, one sound at a time, every day.
“His compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.”
Lamentations 3:22–23 · KJV
Each morning is a fresh start. Yesterday’s missed lesson does not cancel today’s.
“Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.”
Romans 12:2 · KJV
Daily practice renews the mind. Short sessions spread over many days help memory keep new words far longer than one long session.
“The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.”
Proverbs 13:4 · KJV
Wishing to speak French is not enough; steady, diligent work is what bears fruit.
“And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.”
Colossians 3:23 · KJV
Study with your whole heart, as an offering, not only to pass an exam.
“They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.”
Isaiah 40:31 · KJV
When you feel tired, ask for strength and keep going.
A prayer before you study
Heavenly Father, thank You for this new day and for the gift of learning.
I lay before You my laziness, my distractions, my worries and every excuse that keeps me from my study.
Give me discipline to sit down, open this lesson and finish it. Quiet my phone, my mind and my heart, so that my whole being can focus on what I am learning.
Open my ears to hear French clearly, train my mouth to speak it, and strengthen my memory to keep every word You help me learn.
When I feel discouraged or slow, remind me that You are faithful and that small steps taken daily lead to great progress.
I commit this study time to You. Let it bring glory to Your name and open the doors You have prepared for me.
Lord, I know that learning French and becoming a bilingual follower of Your Son, Jesus Christ, will open the doors You have prepared ahead of me, full of abundance and amazing things beyond what I can imagine and what humanity can comprehend. For I know this is the beginning of overflowing blessings in my life.
In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Powerful prayers for your study journey
Prayer for a strong memory and understanding
Lord, You formed my mind and You know how it works. Sharpen my memory today. Help me remember every word, every sound and every rule I study, and bring them back to me when I need them. Give me understanding beyond my own ability, as You gave wisdom to Daniel and his friends. Let nothing I learn today be wasted. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Daniel 1:17 · James 1:5
Prayer to break laziness and procrastination
Father, I refuse to be ruled by laziness or by “later”. I break every habit of putting off what I should do today. Fill me with fresh energy and holy discipline. When my body wants to rest and my mind wants to wander, help me stand up, open my lesson and finish what I started. Make me diligent like the ant that prepares in season. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Proverbs 6:6–8 · 2 Timothy 1:7
Prayer against distractions and a wandering mind
Lord Jesus, I bring every distraction under Your authority: my phone, noise, worries, social media and restless thoughts. Guard my eyes and my attention. Set a hedge around this study time so that nothing steals it. Keep my mind fixed on what is true, useful and good, and give me a peace that keeps me focused. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Philippians 4:7–8 · Isaiah 26:3
Prayer for courage, confidence and exam day
God of all strength, take away fear, shame and the voice that says I am too old, too slow or not good enough. Give me confidence to speak, even with mistakes. On exam day, calm my heart, clear my mind and let me remember everything I have prepared. I trust You with the result, because You open doors that no one can shut. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Joshua 1:9 · Revelation 3:8
Prayer of the power of your faith in God
Almighty God, nothing is too hard for You. Today I choose faith over fear and belief over doubt. I believe that You hear me when I pray and that You reward those who diligently seek You. Let my faith, even if it is as small as a mustard seed, move every mountain between me and this language: fear, forgetfulness, slow progress and every doubt about my future. I speak to those mountains in Jesus’ name and command them to move. I receive Your answer by faith before I see it, and I will keep studying until I hold it in my hands. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Hebrews 11:6 · Matthew 17:20 · Jeremiah 32:27
Prayer of dedication
Heavenly Father, I give You this language, this journey and this dream. Use every word I learn to bless others, to serve in Your kingdom and to provide for my family. Let my progress be a testimony of Your faithfulness. I declare that I will not give up, because You who began this good work in me will carry it on to completion. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Philippians 1:6 · Proverbs 16:3
Always remember, “What God cannot do doesn’t exist. So faith it until you make it,” {{ welcomeName }}!

Before you study · every session
Read the Study method & TCF strategy first
Read every word shown in this WebApp. Know the study method and the TCF strategy before you start your Foundation, and come back to them every time you study.
This WebApp is built for fast-track French. Study at least 2 hours every day to reach B2 — and go beyond to C1.
Two months before your TCF exam date, double it to 4 hours a day. Spend more of that time in the Practice Tests Set and strengthen your Expression orale & Expression écrite.
After your first month of study, start practising your Introduction & about me every day, so you can speak it to the examiner fluently and clearly, in a natural voice, not a recited one.
Finish every French Daily Class topic and answer all 30 TCF-style questions in each day, so you get real practice-test exposure while you study and review.
No sound? Turn the media volume up with the volume keys while a line is playing — that is a separate volume from the ringer. Also check silent mode and, if you use Bluetooth, that the phone is not sending audio to another device.
No French voice is installed on this device, so the play buttons stay silent — reading French through an English voice would teach you the wrong pronunciation. Install a French voice and playback starts working straight away. Android: Settings → System → Languages → Text-to-speech → install French. iPhone / iPad: Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices → French. Windows: Settings → Time & language → Speech → Add voices → French. Mac: System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System voice → Manage voices → French. Reload the page afterwards.

Step 1 · How to read the "Say it" guides
Each line shows a simple sound-by-sound guide like bohn-ZHOOR. Hyphens split the syllables. Read it like English — no special training needed.
CAPITALS
the syllable you say a little louder — bohn-ZHOOR
zh
like the s in "pleasure"
ay · eh · oh
like "say", "bed", "go"
oo
like "food"
ew
the French u — say "ee" with rounded lips
uh
like the a in "about"
ahn · ohn · an
nasal sounds — let the air out through your nose, don't say the n
r
a soft gargle from the back of the throat — never rolled

Your level · CEFR A1 to C2 · estimated

My French level

This estimate updates with every TCF question you answer, in any class day topic or practice set. Each answer is weighted by its CEFR level and corrected for guessing, and your level can never rise above the highest level of questions you have answered (only A1 and A2 questions keep you at A2 at most), then placed on the official TCF scale: 100–199 A1, 200–299 A2, 300–399 B1, 400–499 B2, 500–599 C1, 600–699 C2. Listening and reading convert to NCLC with IRCC’s TCF Canada chart (NCLC 7 = listening 458, reading 453). Writing is scored out of 20 from the answers you Save, on the same IRCC chart (NCLC 7 = 10/20); speaking is not scored here.

TCF Canada · Compréhension orale

Listening Practice Tests

The real test has 39 questions in 35 minutes. Each recording is heard once, then four options appear with one correct answer, and difficulty rises as you go. Each set has 20 progressive items; allow about 18 minutes. Play each recording once, answer, then study the transcript with its sound guide.

Expression orale · Tâche 3

TCF Speaking Practice Tests

Sample TCF test · Expression orale, Tâche 3
L’expression d’un point de vue (giving your point of view)
4 minutes 30, no preparation. The examiner chooses one question and you answer it on your own: say what you think, give reasons and examples, and conclude. The examiner is checking that you can speak spontaneously, continuously and convincingly.
Source: france-education-international.fr/test/tcf-canada
A 4 min 30 plan
·Introduction (about 30 s): repeat the question in your own words and give your position.
·Two or three arguments (about 3 min): each one with a reason and a concrete example.
·One counter-argument, then your answer to it.
·Conclusion (about 30 s): sum up and open the question.

Strategies for the TCF taker

Strategies for the TCF

Advice for all the tests
Before the exam
Find out about the support offered in the center (on computer or on paper), about the conduct of the tests, about their content, about the duration of each test, about the format of the answer sheet (see candidate manual downloadable on the France Éducation international website ).
Practice answering questions according to the medium: tick boxes on an answer sheet (on paper) or click on buttons on the screen (on a computer).
During the examination
1.Read the instructions carefully.
2.Answer all questions.
3.Manage your time well!
Tips for the listening comprehension test
Oral comprehension
Composition and sequence
·The start of a question is indicated to the candidate by a sound signal.
·There are several question formats; discover them in our TCF training.
·The difficulty of the questions increases and their theme changes from one to the next.
·During the listening comprehension test, each question has a set time limit; the next question will move automatically without your intervention. You must wait until the current question has finished.
Attention :
·You will only hear the audio recording and the question once;
·You will hear the question after you have listened to the audio recording;
·The questions are not written in the candidate's booklet.
Before the exam
·Practice switching between topics and staying focused for 30 minutes.
·Practice listening to and understanding audio documents with a single listening.
·Practice answering questions asked after listening to an audio document only once.
·Practice imagining words that could be spoken by characters shown in a photo or drawing.
·While listening to an audio recording, jot down the key words and ideas. Then, gradually, stop noting these words and ideas and practice memorizing them. In everyday life, you don't always have something to write with (paper, pen) to record what you hear. The same is true on exam day.
·While listening to an audio document, practice imagining what questions could be asked about that document.
·While listening to an audio document, practice quickly identifying the communication situation: who is speaking to whom? For what purpose?
During the examination
·You will only hear the audio recording and the question once: so listen carefully.
·For exercises associated with the instruction "Listen to the audio document and the question.", try to read the four answer choices before listening to the audio document.
Tips for the language structures mastery test
Grammar and vocabulary
The exercises in this exam are fill-in-the-blank type. The written instruction in the candidate's booklet is always the same: choose the correct answer.
Before the exam
Practice the exercises provided: remember, there is only one possible answer.
During the examination
You manage your time. You can go back. If you hesitate too long, move on to the next question.
Tips for the reading comprehension test
Reading comprehension
Composition and sequence
The exercises in this test always include:
·a document to read;
·a written question in the candidate's booklet;
·4 answer choices written in the candidate's booklet.
These exercises are all grouped under the instruction: "Read the documents. For each question, choose the correct answer and tick a box on the answer sheet."
Before the exam
Practice the different methods of reading a text: identifying keywords, scanning a text to find specific information, identifying the passage of text on which the question relates, etc.
During the examination
·You manage your time. You can go back. If you hesitate too long, move on to the next question.
·Read the question and the 4 answer choices before reading the text of the document.
Sample TCF test · Expression orale, Tâche 1
L'entretien dirigé (the structured interview)
Bonjour !
Let's review Tâche 1 of TCF Canada, also known as l'entretien dirigé (the structured interview).
Consigne
Le candidat doit faire la preuve de sa capacité à échanger avec une personne qu’il ne connaît pas (l’examinateur).
The candidate must demonstrate the ability to interact with someone they do not know (the examiner).
Themes that may come up · 2-minute interview
Here are some themes that may come up during this 2-minute interview:
·État civil, personnalité, langue(s) parlée(s)
·Famille
·Relations amicales
·Formation et études
·Situation professionnelle ou universitaire
·Activités et habitudes (au travail, à l'université, à la maison, pendant les loisirs, etc.)
·Aptitudes, goûts et centres d'intérêt
·Événements ou activités passés
·Conditions de vie (milieu géographique, logement, environnement socioculturel, équipements, météo, etc.)
·Objets personnels
·Projets, souhaits et désirs
·Déplacements, voyages et itinéraires
·Institutions publiques, infrastructures et associations
Source: france-education-international.fr/…/tcf-tp…
Not a monologue
Contrary to what some people believe, Tâche 1 is not meant to be a monologue. The examiner is supposed to ask you questions. However, some examiners do allow candidates to present their prepared response with little interruption.
In my experience, I took the TCF twice (Jan 2023 in AF Vancouver and Jan 2024 in Ashton Vancouver), and in both exams, the examiner actively asked me questions. So this is nothing new.
To help you prepare, I'm sharing some commonly asked questions (along with sample answers) from the book Réussir le DELF B1. The structure of TCF Canada Tâche 1 is almost identical to DELF B1 – Partie 1.
C1 model answers · one question per theme

My tip
To achieve a solid B2 in this section, try to demonstrate a variety of verb tenses and moods, including the présent, passé composé, imparfait, futur, and conditionnel. The sentences don't need to be very complex: la clé is to answer naturally, speak spontaneously, and show that you're comfortable carrying on a conversation.

How examiners evaluate the speaking section
TCF Canada · Expression orale scoring scale
Ever wondered how TCF Canada examiners evaluate the speaking section?
Here’s a sneak peek into their evaluation criteria sheet. The levels and descriptions are translated below:
Global Scale – Level - Description
C2Can express themselves spontaneously, fluently, and precisely. Can convey subtle nuances of meaning and produce well-structured, clear, and fluid discourse with effective logical organization.
C1Can express him/herself fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for words. Can present a complex subject by integrating secondary arguments and developing particular points to reach an appropriate conclusion.
B2Can communicate with a degree of spontaneity and ease such that a conversation with a native speaker involves no strain for either party. Can highlight important points and details and justify ideas with relevant examples.
B1Can produce simple, coherent speech on familiar topics. Can use a range of simple language to exchange, verify, and confirm information, and respond appropriately.
A2Can communicate using short series of expressions or unconnected phrases in simple tasks requiring a direct and simple exchange of information.
A1Can communicate in a basic way using simple and isolated expressions, provided the conversation partner speaks slowly, clearly, and is cooperative.
Échelle globale – Échelles de production et d’interaction orales générales
Niveau - Descripteur
C2Peut s’exprimer spontanément, très couramment et de façon précise. Peut rendre distinctes de fines nuances de sens et produire un discours élaboré, limpide et fluide, avec une structure logique efficace.
C1Peut s’exprimer spontanément et couramment sans trop apparemment devoir chercher ses mots. Peut présenter un sujet complexe en y intégrant des arguments secondaires et développer des points particuliers pour parvenir à une conclusion appropriée.
B2Peut communiquer avec un degré de spontanéité et d’aisance tel qu’une conversation avec un locuteur natif ne comporte de tension ni pour l’un ni pour l’autre. Peut souligner des points importants et des détails et justifier les idées par des exemples pertinents.
B1Peut assez aisément produire un discours simple et cohérent. Peut exploiter une gamme étendue de langue simple pour échanger, vérifier, confirmer des informations et y réagir.
A2Peut communiquer par de courtes séries d’expressions ou de phrases non articulées, lors de tâches simples ne demandant qu’un échange d’informations simple et direct.
A1Peut communiquer très simplement avec des expressions simples et isolées si l’interlocuteur parle lentement, distinctement et se montre coopératif.
Source: Manuel du Responsable de Session Version AJ, Dec 2024 · scribd.com/…/Manuel-Du-Responsable-de…
